A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same in-context gradient descent work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, proofs, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Appendix G reports original synthetic experiments comparing transformer ICL with directly trained 3-, 4-, and 6-layer networks, including distribution-shift and transformer-depth results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain original synthetic experiments and add results testing changes in the target network's parameter distribution.

M1.justification: The ReLU construction with (2N+4)L layers, its element-wise multiplication component, and the 4L-layer Softmax construction are retained. The new sigmoid example instantiates an existing approximation technique rather than changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds evaluation on 4-layer target networks with parameter distributions N(-0.5,I) and N(0.5,I), extending the tested target-function population. The existing synthetic regression tasks, input-mixture shifts, and longer-context scenarios remain; the diffusion application remains theoretical.

E2.justification: Directly trained 3-, 4-, and 6-layer networks remain the experimental comparators. The added parameter-shift study uses the existing 4-layer network comparator. TINT receives new related-work discussion but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added parameter-shift evaluation fixes inputs at N(-2,Id), uses 4-layer targets, and compares three target-parameter distributions after pretraining with N(0,I) parameters. Existing training budgets, 6,400-sample evaluation, R-squared metric, and baseline training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 also introduces a FLOP comparison without detailed accounting procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2 adds a controlled robustness test of generalization across target-parameter distributions for both transformer variants. Appendix A.4 adds a computational-cost comparison. The earlier input-distribution, context-length, and transformer-depth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average R-squared over 6,400 test samples, and shaded regions already appear in v1's plots. V2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run protocol, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 Figures 5–6 add parameter-shift curves reporting ICL performance comparable to directly trained 4-layer networks. Appendix A.4 newly reports 3.3 billion versus 7.6 billion FLOPs for ICL versus direct 6-layer-network training. These are additional results, not version-to-version performance gains; v1 Figures 1–3 are retained as v2 Figures 3, 4, and 7.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a sigmoid approximation construction with stated constants, and A.4 adds asymptotic computational-cost expressions. V2 also corrects local element-wise multiplication layer indexing. Core guarantees and full proofs remain largely unchanged, although Lemma 4's relevant MLP proof sketch is replaced by a misplaced forward-propagation sketch.

C1.justification: The principal approximation, convergence, and empirical-performance claims remain. The introduction now explicitly restricts generalization to fixed target-network width and depth, and the contribution summary qualifies experimental validation by acknowledging that trained transformers do not always realize the theoretical construction.

C2.justification: V1 principally discusses difficult Softmax weight construction and large transformer dimensions. V2 substantially expands the limitations to cover restricted architectural generalization, theoretical versus practical computational costs, the experiment–construction mismatch, and departures from standard transformer structure. These qualifications materially change how applicability and practical efficiency are interpreted.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a project-specific GitHub link, whereas v1 only links to the upstream implementation. It newly specifies standard-normal target-parameter initialization and 200 hidden dimensions for baseline networks. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that the retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a substantial comparison with Panigrahi et al.'s TINT, positioning the work through explicit construction, gradient coverage, multistep guarantees, and attention type. V2 also adds Hoffmann et al. for computational cost and removes several citations, including the looped-transformer work by Chen et al. and the Softmax-adaptation work by Collins et al.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and substantially reorganizes the narrative: Softmax results and numerical studies receive main-text sections, the conclusion is restructured, informal theorem summaries are removed, and proof sketches and constants are redistributed between the main text and appendices. These are structural changes beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adds the construction schematic in Figure 1 and parameter-shift Figures 5–6, and redisplays existing 6-layer results together in main-text Figure 2. Earlier plots are retained with revised rendering and placement as Figures 3, 4, and 7. The visual exposition is substantially expanded and reorganized.

improvement.justification: The added parameter-shift evidence, explicit applicability limits, closer prior-work comparison, and reproducibility disclosures make the paper easier to assess. These provide a limited improvement around largely unchanged core results. Local regressions temper the gains: Lemma 4 receives a misplaced proof sketch despite retaining its full proof, and the new FLOP comparison lacks detailed accounting.
